text:
Infosys Delivers Steady Q1 Show, Raises Guidance; Time To Buy, Sell Or Hold?
Infosys Share Price
Infosys Share Price: Infosys delivered a strong performance in the June quarter, surpassing Street estimates in terms of revenue, profit growth, and deal wins. The company also revised its FY26 revenue growth guidance to 1–3% from 0–3%, in line with analyst expectations.
However, the muted upgrade in guidance reflects continued softness in organic growth. Commentary remained largely unchanged from the previous quarter, with management flagging ongoing delays in discretionary tech spending and decision-making cycles.

In early trade on Thursday, Infosys was trading in the red, down nearly 1% from Wednesday’s closing price.
Despite the upbeat Q1 performance, analysts note Infosys’s cautious tone. According to Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL), the company continues to see clients adopt a wait-and-watch approach amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and tariff risks. “The macro environment remains unchanged compared to Q4, which is a key reason behind the conservative guidance," MOFSL said. It values the stock at 24x FY27 EPS and maintains a ‘Neutral’ rating with a target price of Rs 1,750, implying an 11% upside.
Nuvama Institutional Equities was more optimistic, citing solid growth and improved quality of revenues due to lower third-party income. While it acknowledged the guidance raise was modest, Nuvama said the outlook is reasonable given global macroeconomic uncertainty. The brokerage has raised its target multiple to 25x FY27 PE (from 24x earlier) and upgraded its target price to Rs 1,850 (from Rs 1,700), retaining a ‘Buy’ rating.
MOFSL also highlighted that although Infosys trimmed its upper-end organic revenue growth guidance by 40 basis points, the actual performance trajectory appears to be improving. The firm now expects Infosys to clock around 2.5% organic growth in FY26, supported by a stronger first half.
Nirmal Bang echoed a mixed sentiment. The firm noted that strong deal wins, AI-led transformation initiatives, and disciplined capital allocation enhance long-term visibility. However, macro uncertainty will likely prevent Infosys from raising its guidance in the second half of FY26, typically the company’s stronger half. “The Q1 beat will be offset by management’s cautious tone, soft organic guidance, and lower third-party revenue, though these factors are balanced by healthy margin expansion, robust order book, and improving free cash flows," it said. Nirmal Bang reiterated a ‘Hold’ rating with a revised target of ₹1,746 (up from ₹1,686).
Looking ahead, Nuvama expects demand conditions to remain weak for the next couple of quarters due to the macro backdrop. However, it remains bullish on the medium-to-long-term outlook, citing high technology debt across enterprises that could trigger a spending rebound once conditions improve. “Infosys is well-positioned to benefit from that recovery. At 21x FY27 PE, valuations remain attractive," Nuvama added, maintaining a ‘Buy/SN’ call.
